0.value:
The dict node is a named store: a collection of entries, each a key and the value filed under it. You put entries in, ask for them back by key, and can save the whole collection to a file and load it again.

A dictionary is a bundle of named values travelling as one thing. Where a list says "three numbers, and you remember what they are", a dictionary says "x is this, y is that, confidence is the other".

The collection is also saved with the patch, so it is still there the next time the patch is opened.

PUTTING ENTRIES IN:
Send a list to 'store': the first element is the key, the rest is the value. "red 255 0 0" files the list 255 0 0 under red. A key with a single value after it files just that value. Sending a whole dictionary to 'store' - or text that starts with { and reads as JSON - replaces the entire collection.

GETTING THEM BACK:
Send a key to 'retrieve by key'. If it is there, its value goes out of 'out';
if not, the key goes out of 'unmatched' instead. Wire 'unmatched' up rather than assuming a lookup succeeded.
A key containing / reaches into nested dictionaries: synth/freq looks up freq inside the dictionary filed under synth.

'retrieve by key' can store too. A list of two or more elements there files everything after the first under the first, always as a list. "delete red" removes red, and "append" followed by a value files the value under the next unused whole number.

SYNTAX:
dict <name>

The name is only the label the node shows. It does not load anything; after a save or load the label shows the file's name.

EXAMPLE:
dict colours

INPUTS and PARAMETERS:

retrieve by key:
A key to look up, or a list to store, as above.

store:
A key followed by its value, a whole dictionary, or JSON text.

load:
Click to choose a JSON file; its contents replace the collection.

save:
Click to choose where to write the collection as a JSON file.

clear:
Empties the collection.

send dict:
Sends the whole collection out of 'dict out'. The collection is kept.

MESSAGES:
These can be sent to any inlet.

keys - send the list of keys out of 'out'
next - send the next entry, as a one-entry dictionary; it stops at the last reset - make next start from the first entry again random - send one entry, chosen at random, as a one-entry dictionary dump - send every entry as a list: the key followed by its value. A value that is a list is spread out after the key; any other value - a number, a string - is one item
search <beginning> - send, as one list, every entry whose value is itself a
dictionary and whose path has a level beginning with the text: each item is the path and the dictionary found there
save <file> / load <file> - save or load without the file dialog
clear - empty the collection

A consequence: an entry whose key is one of these words cannot be stored or looked up by sending a list that starts with it - the word is taken as the message.

OUTPUTS:

out:
The value that was looked up, and the replies to the messages above.

unmatched:
The key, when nothing in the collection matches it.

dict out:
The whole collection, when 'send dict' is clicked.

RELATED:
construct_dict builds a dictionary from inlets, dict_extract and dict_retrieve take one apart, dict_keys lists its keys and dict_stream sends its entries one by one. dict_search finds a branch of a nested dictionary by typing.
